questions.question: Agriculture's contribution to South Africa's GDP is approximately:
The "linkages" argument for agriculture's importance points to:
options: Its supply of raw materials to agro-processing — mills, canneries, refineries, abattoirs
Its control of the taxi industry

questions.question: Which product belongs primarily to South Africa's EXPORT market list?
Agriculture slows rural depopulation because it:
options: Pays the highest wages in the economy
Anchors rural settlement and provides jobs where alternatives barely exist

subtopics.title: Two Farming Worlds: Small-Scale and Large-Scale

questions.question: Which feature belongs to LARGE-SCALE commercial farming?
options: Heavy capital investment and production for market and export

questions.question: Small-scale farmers on communal land struggle to obtain bank loans because:
options: Communal land cannot easily be used as collateral
Banks do not lend to farmers at all
They have too much machinery already

questions.question: The five clean comparison lines for the two farming systems are:
options: Farm size, capital and technology, labour source, market orientation, land tenure
Province, language, crop colour, season, distance

questions.question: A balanced evaluation notes that large-scale farming delivers national food supply and exports BUT:
options: Employs fewer people per hectare as it mechanises

subtopics.title: The Maize Case Study: From Highveld Field to Export Terminal

questions.question: The Maize Triangle spans which provinces?
options: Western Cape, Northern Cape, Eastern Cape

questions.question: Which is a physical factor FAVOURING maize on the highveld?
options: Summer rainfall of roughly 500–800 mm in the growing season

questions.question: Maize "feeds the nation twice" because:
options: It is planted twice a year
White maize is the human staple and yellow maize is the base of animal feed
It is exported and then re-imported
Both leaves and roots are eaten

questions.question: The chief hindering factor for maize production is:
options: Rainfall variability and recurring drought in the summer-rainfall interior
A shortage of land in the Free State

subtopics.title: Food Security: The Framework, the Factors, the Fixes

questions.question: The clause "physical AND economic access" in the food security definition means:
options: Food must exist nearby AND be affordable
Food must be imported and exported
Transport is irrelevant to food security

questions.question: South Africa's food security paradox is that the country is:
options: Food insecure nationally but secure in every household
Unable to produce staples at all
Food secure only in drought years
Food secure at national level while millions of households are food insecure

questions.question: Which trio lists ECONOMIC factors influencing food security?
options: Unemployment, food price inflation, input costs

questions.question: The National School Nutrition Programme is best classified as:
options: A production-side strategy increasing maize yields
An access-side intervention feeding around nine million learners

subtopics.title: The Country That Runs on Pap

questions.question: Maize appears on the supper plate "twice" because:
options: Pap is served in two helpings
It is visible as pap and hidden in the chicken raised on maize feed
Maize is both starch and protein
White and yellow maize taste the same

questions.question: The silos beside the railway lines in the grain belt represent:
options: The support infrastructure a crop this size requires

questions.question: "Thunderstorms are gamblers" captures the risk that:
options: Summer rain sometimes fails entirely, bringing drought to the whole triangle

questions.question: In a drought year, rising maize prices hurt the poorest families first because:
options: Pap is the staple food of tight budgets

questions.question: On the five-finger comparison, "hired workers against the family" is the line for:
The fair evaluation of the small farm is that it:
options: Sustains millions of families but has low yields that leave households exposed
Produces most of the nation's supermarket food

questions.question: "The bridge, not the fence" refers to policies that:
options: Replace all small farms with large ones
Help small farmers grow toward commercial production through finance, tenure, training and market access

questions.question: Secure land rights help small farmers grow because they:
options: Allow the plot to back a loan, unlocking finance

questions.question: The resolution of the "full silos, empty plates" riddle is:
options: South Africa produces too little food nationally
National supply is adequate but poverty blocks household access

questions.question: A family in front of stocked shelves with no money to buy is:
options: Food secure because food is present
Outside the definition of food security
Food insecure — economic access has failed

questions.question: The "three bags" of food security causes are:
Which fix is correctly matched to its target?
options: Drought-tolerant seed — aimed at the money bag
School feeding — aimed at the nature bag
Food gardens at homes and schools — shortening the distance between soil and plate
